facts.claim: The National Cyber Crime Helpline number is 1930.
facts.source: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, I4C (cybercrime.gov.in)
facts.headline: Helpline: 1930

facts.claim: You can also report cybercrime online at cybercrime.gov.in.
facts.source: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, I4C (cybercrime.gov.in)
facts.headline: Report online

facts.claim: If money is lost to a fraud, report it immediately, because early reporting helps authorities act.
facts.source: I4C public awareness advisory on financial fraud
facts.headline: Report immediately

facts.claim: Digital arrest is a scam. No police officer or agency arrests anyone, or demands money, over a phone or video call.
facts.source: MHA / I4C public advisory on digital arrest scams
facts.headline: Digital arrest is a SCAM

facts.claim: Scammers create fear, urgency and secrecy. Pause, hang up, and talk to someone you trust.
facts.source: I4C public awareness advisory on cyber frauds
facts.headline: Pause. Hang up. Talk.

facts.claim: Never share your OTP, UPI PIN or card details. You never need a PIN to receive money.
facts.source: RBI / NPCI public awareness advisory on digital payment fraud
facts.headline: Never share OTP or PIN

facts.claim: Genuine employers do not ask for registration fees or security deposits for a job.
facts.source: I4C public awareness advisory on fake job offers
facts.headline: Real jobs never ask for fees

facts.claim: If someone threatens you online, do not pay. Save the chats, block the account and report it. It is not your fault.
facts.source: I4C public awareness advisory on sextortion
facts.headline: Not your fault. Don't pay.
